about: Every mutant was applied to the file as it is at base_commit, which the change that adds this record does not change. killer is the first test nextest reported failing (it stops at the first failure, with tests running in parallel, so another failing test may be reported first on another run). killer_at says where that test function exists: base, or this_commit for a test the change that adds this record adds. A test that exists at base may still kill only through cases that change adds to it: before_this_change gives the verdict at base where it differs. Each mutant that survived its filtered run at base was run again at base against every bridge test (the whole_set run) before it was called a survivor. Every survivor left at this_commit is listed in accepted_survivors with its reason: an equivalent one is marked equivalent, and one that is not says why it is not killed yet. A hand-written mutant's mutation id is the first 32 hex digits of the SHA-256 of its edits in order, each as its from text, a NUL byte, its to text and a NUL byte, in UTF-8. A tool mutant is named as cargo-mutants --list names it, by line and column. Every run was on base_commit, with the file and its test module byte for byte as there (or as this change leaves the test module, for survivors_again). A tool mutant that survived was run again in the whole_set and survivors_again runs as the same edit written as text, under the id named in its run's command.

runs.command: each mutant's edits applied as exact text, then cargo nextest run --locked -p bridge -E 'test(/transfer|skip|withdraw|contra|responses|failure_code|statement|verif/)'

as the hand run with every bridge test (-E 'all()', --no-fail-fast for the batch), for the tool's three missed mutants (T1 is 312:21, T2 is 604:5 with Some(""), T3 is 604:5 with Some("xyzzy")) and the thirty-six hand-written ones that survived. T1, T2, T3, X15, X20 and X24 were each run alone; X69 was run alone (its edit overlaps X68's) and the other thirty-two were applied together as one batch of independent edits that touch no common text, and a batch that passes every test means each edit passes every test alone. X82 and X86 each first read caught by financial_mode_tests::a_draining_refusal_after_part_of_the_standard_read_was_sent_is_not_waited_out, a test of another module that failed alone; the batch, which has both edits, passed all 5079 tests, and that is the verdict recorded

as the hand run for the same thirty-nine, with -E 'test(/agent_import::transfers::tests/)' (the 47 tests of the module, the only module whose tests can see these edits, and a killer is a test failing there); then the seven still missed (X82, X86, X93, X107, X110, X118, X121) applied together as one batch against every bridge test (5096), which passed

X82.reason: equivalent: the batch sent is the journal's own latest record, so reading it again merges unchanged with the record already read (a changed record would raise BatchRecordChanged in the fold, which this edit does not touch), and the double-booking check reads only the statement's bank, the lineage and the references, never a status, so the subject batch named or not gives the same pairs

X86.reason: equivalent, unreachable: the held view is read only when the build withdraws a skip, which is when the build needs the view, so this edit would admit where base refuses; but a held skip comes from the journal's map of skip keys (no key twice) and is checked for a positive amount and two different ledgers when it is saved, so held_carrier_view never fails for a saved journal

X93.reason: not killed, and not equivalent: any and all differ only when one refusal lists rows from two or more batches and only some of them were restored, which needs a journal with a recorded rollback covering one of two batches that carry skipped rows; no fixture here builds that journal, and a refusal with one batch, or with every batch restored or none, reads the same under both

X107.reason: equivalent: the only pairs read from the view with the build in it are RefuseAtBuild pairs, which are two equal references from two statements and do not depend on the date, so one more day either side of the build lists the same pairs

X110.reason: equivalent: the company GUID is compared case-insensitively, and canonical_batch_guid only fixes the case, so a lower or upper case GUID in the saved line reaches the same facts and the same section; the upper-case test passes on base and on this mutant

X118.reason: equivalent: the early return only avoids reads for a batch about no transfers, and no check can refuse a batch that carries no transfer, so the full admission returns the same None
